newsitem.title: USA: Dollar gains as stocks rally, Bundesbank holds rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Dollar gains as stocks rally, Bundesbank holds rates steady.

text.p: The dollar ended higher on Tuesday after the German central bank elected to keep interest rates unchanged and Wall Street stocks posted significant gains for a second consecutive day.
Analysts had suspected the Bundesbank might switch its key money market rate, know as the repurchase rate or "repo," from its current fixed level of 3.0 percent to a variable rate.

This would have represented a de facto rise in interest rates and supported the mark by making German assets denominated in marks relatively But the Bundesbank kept its key rate unchanged and cooled talk that it might push up interest rates at an upcoming policy meeting on Thursday by also announcing a sharp slowdown in M3 money supply growth -- an indicator the central bank uses to gauge future inflation.

"The Bundesbank kept its repo at a fixed rate and that took any potential for dollar selling out of the market right there," said Stephen Flanagan, vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Credit Agricole Indosuez.
The dollar ended the day at 1.8405 marks, a full pfennig up from 1.8305 on Monday. It also edged up to 118.20 yen from 117.82.
The dollar drifted down from its highs of the day after a meeting of the Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee yielded no change in U.S. interest rates.
But the Fed's decision to keep the key federal funds rate steady at its current level of 5.50 percent was widely expected and the damage to the dollar proved limited.

"It would have been a shocker if they had actually done something on rates and it looks like the dollar just consolidated some of its gains," said Ricardo Gomes, foreign exchange manager at Republic National Bank of New York.
After slipping from early highs following the Fed's decision on rates, the Dow Jones industrial average battled back to end up 115 points at 7,918.

Dealers said that Tuesday's stock gains, taken together with Monday's 109 point advance, helped reassure a nervous currency market that last Friday's mammoth 247-point retreat was not the beginning of large and lengthy downturn in stocks.
"As long as the stock market remains positive the dollar should remain well bid," said Hillel Waxman, chief foreign exchange dealer at Bank Leumi Trust Co. of New York.
Dollar gains against the yen were capped indirectly by active buying of yen for marks and by nervousness ahead of U.S. trade figures for June, due to be released Wednesday.

The total U.S. trade deficit, which stood at roughly $10 billion in May, is expected to edge up slightly, and traders said a large increase in the bilateral gap with Japan could fuel buying of yen for dollars.
In other trade Tuesday, the dollar retreated to 1.5137 Swiss francs from 1.5170 on Monday and slipped to Canadian $1.3942 from C$1.3883. The British pound ended unchanged at $1.6060.
